sourceSnapshot.note: Names and category membership are a snapshot of the Handbook index. This is a study list, not an endorsement, ranking, or exhaustive list of all products in each market.

groups.title: Relational, distributed SQL, key-value, document, and wide-column stores

technologies.name: PostgreSQL
technologies.role: General-purpose relational database; evaluate transaction, indexing, extension, operations, and workload fit.

technologies.name: MySQL
technologies.role: General-purpose relational database; evaluate its engine, compatibility, operations, and workload fit.

technologies.name: Spanner
technologies.role: Distributed relational database service; examine geographic consistency, latency, and service-specific operating model.

technologies.name: CockroachDB
technologies.role: Distributed SQL database; examine transaction semantics, topology, latency, and operating complexity.

technologies.name: TiDB
technologies.role: Distributed SQL platform; evaluate SQL compatibility, storage/compute layout, workload mix, and operations.

technologies.name: Vitess
technologies.role: MySQL sharding and database-cluster management layer; compare an application-facing sharding platform with a distributed SQL database.

technologies.name: YugabyteDB
technologies.role: Distributed SQL database; evaluate its compatibility model, consistency, regions, and operational footprint.

technologies.name: Redis
technologies.role: In-memory data platform used for cache and other low-latency data structures; evaluate persistence, memory cost, and data-loss behavior for the chosen mode.

technologies.name: Memcached
technologies.role: In-memory cache focused on simple key-value caching; compare its intentionally narrower responsibilities with a broader data platform.

technologies.name: DynamoDB
technologies.role: Managed key-value/document database; model access patterns, partition keys, consistency options, and provider-specific limits.

technologies.name: MongoDB
technologies.role: Document database; evaluate document boundaries, indexes, transaction needs, and query patterns.

technologies.name: Cassandra
technologies.role: Distributed wide-column database; design around partition-key access patterns and replication behavior.

technologies.name: ScyllaDB
technologies.role: Distributed wide-column database with documented Cassandra/CQL compatibility; check its versioned compatibility matrix because support is not a blanket promise of identical behavior.

technologies.name: Bigtable
technologies.role: Managed wide-column database; evaluate key design, range access, and managed-service constraints.

technologies.name: HBase
technologies.role: Wide-column database in the Hadoop ecosystem; evaluate its deployment and integration needs against the workload.

groups.comparison: Do not rank these products on a single scalability label. First separate relational transactions, distributed SQL, application-managed sharding, cache/key-value access, document retrieval, and wide-column access patterns. Then compare consistency, indexing/query flexibility, partition-key constraints, operational model, failure behavior, migration cost, and measured workload.

groups.title: Analytical, time-series, graph, and search systems

technologies.name: BigQuery
technologies.role: Managed analytical warehouse; evaluate scan-oriented query economics, governance, and cloud integration.

technologies.name: ClickHouse
technologies.role: Column-oriented analytical database; evaluate ingest, aggregation, compression, and query patterns.

technologies.name: Snowflake
technologies.role: Managed analytical data platform; evaluate workload isolation, governance, ecosystem, and cost model.

technologies.name: Redshift
technologies.role: Managed analytical warehouse; evaluate its architecture and integration in the selected cloud environment.

technologies.name: Druid
technologies.role: Analytical data store often used for interactive time-oriented aggregates; assess ingestion and query pattern fit.

technologies.name: Pinot
technologies.role: Distributed OLAP store focused on low-latency analytical queries; assess freshness and indexing needs.

technologies.name: InfluxDB
technologies.role: Time-series database; evaluate write, query, retention, and downsampling requirements against its current edition.

technologies.name: TimescaleDB
technologies.role: Time-series capabilities built around PostgreSQL; compare relational integration with specialized time-series operations.

technologies.name: VictoriaMetrics
technologies.role: Time-series monitoring storage; evaluate ingestion, retention, query compatibility, and operational design.

technologies.name: Neo4j
technologies.role: Property-graph database; evaluate relationship traversal patterns, graph model, and query needs.

technologies.name: Elasticsearch
technologies.role: Search and analytics engine; evaluate indexing, relevance, aggregations, operations, and document freshness.

technologies.name: OpenSearch
technologies.role: Open search and analytics suite; compare its current distribution, plugins, compatibility, and operating model with alternatives.

groups.comparison: Choose by query shape and freshness: broad scans and aggregates, event-time windows, multi-hop relationship traversal, or relevance-ranked text retrieval are different workloads. Keep authoritative business records separate from rebuildable analytics/search projections and define reconciliation, freshness, retention, and access control.

groups.title: Vector databases, nearest-neighbor libraries, and embedded storage

technologies.name: Pinecone
technologies.role: Managed vector database; evaluate managed operations, filtering, freshness, tenancy, and cost.

technologies.name: Weaviate
technologies.role: Vector database platform; compare deployment and data-model capabilities against the retrieval workload.

technologies.name: Milvus
technologies.role: Vector database; evaluate index, deployment, scaling, and operational requirements.

technologies.name: Qdrant
technologies.role: Vector search engine; evaluate filtering, deployment, index choices, and workload needs.

technologies.name: Faiss
technologies.role: Vector similarity-search library; compare embedding search as an application-managed component with a full database service.

technologies.name: pgvector
technologies.role: Vector extension for PostgreSQL; compare keeping vectors beside relational data with a separate vector system.

technologies.name: RocksDB
technologies.role: Embeddable key-value storage engine based on an LSM design; distinguish an embedded library from a distributed database service.

groups.comparison: For vector workloads compare managed service versus self-operated database versus embedded library; exact versus approximate search; recall versus latency; filtering and tenant isolation; update/delete freshness; index rebuild time; and total memory/storage cost. For embedded storage, compare application ownership and replication/recovery work rather than assuming a library supplies distributed-system behavior.

groups.title: Messaging, streaming, change capture, and workflow platforms

technologies.name: Kafka
technologies.role: Distributed event log and streaming platform; evaluate partition ordering, retention, consumer replay, and operations.

technologies.name: RabbitMQ
technologies.role: Message broker with routing and acknowledgement patterns; evaluate delivery workflow, topology, and operational fit.

technologies.name: NATS
technologies.role: Messaging system with core and persistence-oriented options; compare latency, retention, and delivery needs by mode.

technologies.name: SQS
technologies.role: Managed queue service; evaluate delivery, visibility, ordering options, quotas, and provider dependency.

technologies.name: Kinesis
technologies.role: Managed streaming service; evaluate shard/throughput model, retention, consumers, and provider integration.

technologies.name: Pulsar
technologies.role: Distributed messaging and streaming platform; compare its topic, subscription, storage, and operations model to requirements.

technologies.name: Flink
technologies.role: Stream-processing engine; evaluate event-time stateful processing, checkpointing, and operational complexity.

technologies.name: Spark
technologies.role: Data-processing engine with batch and streaming capabilities; compare latency and processing semantics for the use case.

technologies.name: Debezium
technologies.role: Change-data-capture platform based on database change streams/logs; evaluate connector support, schema changes, and replay behavior.

technologies.name: Temporal
technologies.role: Durable workflow orchestration platform; evaluate long-running stateful workflows, retries, and operational model.

technologies.name: Airflow
technologies.role: Workflow scheduler/orchestrator commonly used for data pipelines; compare scheduled DAG execution with event-driven long-running workflows.

groups.comparison: Separate a work queue, retained event log, pub/sub delivery, stream processor, CDC connector, and workflow engine. They solve related but different problems. Compare ordering scope, retention/replay, acknowledgement, redelivery, state/checkpointing, backpressure, scheduling, failure recovery, and operator burden. A broker guarantee does not make an external business side effect exactly once.

groups.title: Coordination, service discovery, proxies, and service meshes

technologies.name: ZooKeeper
technologies.role: Coordination service used for metadata and leader/membership patterns; evaluate quorum operations and client semantics.

technologies.name: etcd
technologies.role: Distributed key-value store commonly used for coordination/configuration; evaluate consistency, watch, and quorum behavior.

technologies.name: Consul
technologies.role: Service networking and discovery platform; distinguish its catalog, health, and service-mesh responsibilities.

technologies.name: Nginx
technologies.role: Web server and reverse proxy; evaluate routing, TLS, caching, and configuration needs.

technologies.name: Envoy
technologies.role: Programmable proxy used for service and edge traffic; evaluate dynamic configuration, protocol support, and operations.

technologies.name: HAProxy
technologies.role: Load balancer and proxy; evaluate transport/application routing, health, and deployment needs.

technologies.name: Kong
technologies.role: API gateway platform; compare gateway policy and plugin requirements with a general-purpose proxy.

technologies.name: Istio
technologies.role: Service-mesh platform; evaluate identity, traffic policy, telemetry, sidecar/control-plane complexity, and alternatives.

technologies.name: Linkerd
technologies.role: Service-mesh platform; compare its operating model and feature scope against the actual service-network requirements.

groups.comparison: First decide whether the need is naming/discovery, consensus-backed coordination, connection balancing, HTTP routing, API policy, or service-to-service identity/telemetry. A mesh can centralize some network policy but adds control-plane and data-plane components. A proxy is not automatically an API gateway, and a service catalog is not consensus for business data.

groups.title: Observability, CDN/edge, and object delivery

technologies.name: Prometheus
technologies.role: Metrics collection and query ecosystem; evaluate scrape/push patterns, label cardinality, and retention architecture.

technologies.name: Grafana
technologies.role: Visualization and observability interface; distinguish dashboards from the telemetry storage and collection layers.

technologies.name: Jaeger
technologies.role: Distributed tracing backend/UI; compare trace ingestion, sampling, storage, and query requirements.

technologies.name: OpenTelemetry
technologies.role: Vendor-neutral instrumentation and telemetry data model/protocol ecosystem; it is not itself a telemetry database.

technologies.name: Cloudflare
technologies.role: Edge network and security platform; evaluate CDN, DNS, proxy, security, and edge-compute needs separately.

technologies.name: CloudFront
technologies.role: AWS content-delivery network; evaluate origin integration, cache policy, invalidation, and geographic distribution.

technologies.name: Akamai
technologies.role: Content delivery and security platform; compare delivery footprint, controls, and contract/operating requirements.

technologies.name: Fastly
technologies.role: Programmable content-delivery platform; evaluate caching, edge logic, purge behavior, and delivery needs.

technologies.name: S3
technologies.role: AWS object-storage service; evaluate object semantics, lifecycle, access, consistency contract, durability, and provider-specific limits.

groups.comparison: Separate instrumentation and transport from collection, storage, query, and visualization. For CDN/edge compare cache control, key design, purge, origin shielding, security, and programmable compute. For object storage compare immutable object delivery and lifecycle against transactional database requirements; do not assume S3 semantics transfer identically to another provider.

groups.title: Realtime delivery and API protocols

technologies.name: Firebase
technologies.role: Google's application-development platform including realtime data capabilities; identify the specific product/service and consistency/security model before comparing.

technologies.name: gRPC
technologies.role: RPC framework/protocol based on HTTP/2 and Protocol Buffers in common deployments; evaluate generated contracts, streaming, browser support, and observability.

technologies.name: GraphQL
technologies.role: API query language/runtime that lets clients request shaped data; evaluate authorization, query-cost limits, caching, and N+1 behavior.

technologies.name: WebSockets
technologies.role: Bidirectional persistent communication channel; evaluate connection scale, reconnection, ordering, authorization, and application-level delivery guarantees.

groups.comparison: Choose an API contract and delivery mechanism from caller needs: resource-oriented HTTP, schema-driven query, typed RPC, or persistent realtime channel. For server push also compare Server-Sent Events, long polling, webhooks, and WebSockets; they differ in direction, connection state, retry, firewall compatibility, and delivery guarantees.
